summary.text: Son of Merops (`merops-percote`) of Percote, co-captain with Araphius of the men of Adrasteia and Apaesus — a namesake of the Argive king of the Seven against Thebes, but Homer fixes this man among the Trojan allies whom black fate led to war despite their father's prophetic counsel.

story.text: Nestor's muster-roll names Adrastus and Araphius, sons twain of Merops, skilled in prophecy above all men, who would not suffer his sons to go into war; but the twain would in no wise hearken, for the fates of black death were leading them on.
When Hector pressed the Achaeans back, the Trojans took a chariot and two men, the best of their people — the sons of Merops — and these the son of Tydeus, Diomedes, slew.
